chunks: Say: 'Have you seen your partners whom you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created of the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens? Or have We given them a book so they are upon clear evidence from it? No, the polytheists promise one another only delusion.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three proofs against the polytheists' idols mentioned in Surah Al-Furqan?
ai.summary: Although the verse is from Surah Yasin (36:60), it serves as a pivotal argument in Shia tafsir against the attribution of independent creative power (khalq) to idols or other divine agents, reinforcing the concept of Tawhid al-Afal. The rhetorical challenge emphasizes that polytheists possess no clear evidence (bayyinah) from a divine book, highlighting the contrast between their baseless claims and the clear monotheism of the Quran. This verse is often cited to refute the idea of intercession by created beings who lack their own authority.
